title: Annotatio III §.II: Second Consociation attempt ranked WITTENBERGENSE — Formula explains Coena consensus; eleven Reformed and six Lutheran subscribers; almost Interim-like pending wider approval
pass_a_gloss: For that reason I judge this Second Consociation Effort more perfect, the WITTENBERG one, on account of the Wittenberg Formula of Concord, which also explains the Consensus in the Dogma concerning the Supper, subscribed by eleven theologians of the Reformed party and six of the Lutheran, and to be read in Chytraeus pp. 680–681; even if it is almost to be called Interim-like, because those theologians (Chytraeus’s words) did not want to conclude that Concord altogether before they had also referred it to the remaining Theologians and Magistrates, as something to be approved by them as well.
pass_b_english: On that account I rank this second Consociation attempt higher — the Wittenberg one — because of the Wittenberg Formula of Concord, which even spells out agreement on the doctrine of the Supper.
Eleven Reformed and six Lutheran theologians subscribed it; read it in Chytraeus, pp. 680–681.

Call it almost Interim-like if you like: those theologians (Chytraeus’s words) would not finish the Concord until they had also referred it to the other theologians and magistrates for their approval.
source_text: Perfectius eo nomine reputandum duco Molimen hoc Consociationis Secundum, WITTENBERGENSE, ob Formulam Concordiae Wittenbergensem, etiam Consensum in Dogmate de Coena explicantem, ab undecim Reformatae, & sex Lutheranae partis Theologis subscriptam, legendamque apud Chytraeum pag. 680. 681.; Utut Interimisticum quasi dicendum, quòd Concordiam illam (sunt verba Chytraei) non concludere omninò voluerint dicti Theologi, priusquam ad caeteros etiam Theologos & Magistratus, eam, ceu ab his quoque approbandam, retulissent.

choices.why: pending referral for approval, not final lock
rejected: the Augsburg Interim itself as identical

notes: Hexades Annotatio III §.II densify §204; WITTENBERGENSE ranking and Interimistic caveat.
